title: Compatible Cohen power-series presentations of a complete local map
statement: Let $f:(A,\mathfrak m_A)\to(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], both complete for their maximal-ideal-adic topologies [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Then there are complete regular local rings $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ and $(S,\mathfrak m_S)$, surjective local maps $q:R\to A$ and $v:S\to B$, and a local map $u:R\to S$ with $vu=fq$, such that $R$ and $S$ are formal power-series rings [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] over fields if $A/\mathfrak m_A$ has characteristic zero and over Cohen rings [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] if it has characteristic $p>0$. One can choose a regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $R$ whose images in $S$ extend to a regular system of parameters of $S$, with $t_1=p$ in residue characteristic $p$. The map $R\to S$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NN (lemma-embed-map-Noetherian-complete-local-rings), statement and proof; the choice $t_1=p$ is made in the proof of Proposition Tag 07NQ (proposition-fs-flat-fibre-fs)

proof.text: (Presentations of $A$ and $B$.) Since $f$ is local it induces a field homomorphism $A/\mathfrak m_A\to B/\mathfrak m_B$, so the two residue fields have the same characteristic. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-power-series-presentation] to $A$ and to $B$: there are $n,e\ge0$, coefficient rings $\Lambda_A,\Lambda_B$ which are both fields (residue characteristic $0$) or both Cohen rings [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] (residue characteristic $p>0$), and surjective local homomorphisms $q:R=\Lambda_A[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]\to A$ and $v_0:S_0=\Lambda_B[[Z_1,\ldots,Z_e]]\to B$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The same node says $R$ is a complete regular local ring with regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ equal to $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ ($d=n$) in the field case and to $t_1=p,t_2=X_1,\ldots,t_d=X_n$ ($d=n+1$) in the Cohen case. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] (1),(3) applied to $\Lambda_B$, $S_0$ is local with $\mathfrak m_{S_0}=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_e)$ resp. $(p,Z_1,\ldots,Z_e)$ and is $\mathfrak m_{S_0}$-adically complete. As $v_0$ is surjective and local, $v_0^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)$ is a maximal ideal containing $\mathfrak m_{S_0}$, hence equals $\mathfrak m_{S_0}$; so $J=\ker v_0\subseteq\mathfrak m_{S_0}$ and $v_0(\mathfrak m_{S_0}^m)=\mathfrak m_B^m$ for all $m$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NN (lemma-embed-map-Noetherian-complete-local-rings), proof

proof.text: (Lifting $fq$ to $\varphi:R\to S_0$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-field-cohen-power-series-formally-smooth] (case (i) with $\Lambda_A$ a field of characteristic $0$, case (ii) with $\Lambda_A$ a Cohen ring), $\mathbf Z\to R$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_R$-adic topology. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-into-complete] with base ring $\mathbf Z$ (every ring is a $\mathbf Z$-algebra and every ring map is $\mathbf Z$-linear), source $R$ with $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_R$, target $S_0$ with $I=\mathfrak m_{S_0}$ (complete by step 1), the ideal $J$ with $t=1$ ($J\subseteq I$ by step 1), and $g=fq:R\to B\cong S_0/J$, which satisfies $g(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B=v_0(I)$ (so $r=1$) because $q$ and $f$ are local. $J$ is closed: $v_0$ maps $\bigcap_m(J+\mathfrak m_{S_0}^m)$ into $\bigcap_m\mathfrak m_B^m$, which is $0$ because $B$ is $\mathfrak m_B$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] (the map $B\to\varprojlim B/\mathfrak m_B^m$ is injective); so this intersection lies in $\ker v_0=J$, and it contains $J$. The lemma gives a ring map $\varphi:R\to S_0$ with $v_0\varphi=fq$ and $\varphi(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_{S_0}$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NN, proof, second paragraph ('We lift the composition ... by Lemma 07NL and Lemma 07NJ')

proof.text: (The ring $S$ and the maps $v$, $u$.) Put $S=\Lambda_B[[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n,Z_1,\ldots,Z_e]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], a power series ring over the field resp. Cohen ring $\Lambda_B$, and regard $S_0\subseteq S$ as the series not involving the $Y_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] with $n+e$ variables, $S$ is a Noetherian $\mathfrak m_S$-adically complete regular local ring with $\mathfrak m_S=(Y,Z)$ resp. $(p,Y,Z)$ and $\dim S=n+e$ resp. $n+e+1$; in particular $\mathfrak m_{S_0}\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-quotient-variables] ($i=n$) the map $\pi:S\to S_0$ setting $Y_i=0$ is a surjective ring map which is the identity on $S_0$; put $v=v_0\pi:S\to B$, surjective, and local since $v(Y_i)=0$, $v(Z_j)=v_0(Z_j)\in\mathfrak m_B$ and $v(p)=p\cdot1_B=v_0(p)\in\mathfrak m_B$ in the Cohen case. Let $u:R\to S$ be the map of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] with $C=\Lambda_A$, $T=S$, $\alpha=\varphi|_{\Lambda_A}$, $I=\mathfrak m_S$, $b_i=\varphi(X_i)+Y_i\in\mathfrak m_S$ (step 2 gives $\varphi(X_i)\in\mathfrak m_{S_0}$); it is continuous, and local because $u(X_i)\in\mathfrak m_S$ and, in the Cohen case, $u(p)=p\in\mathfrak m_S$, and these generate $\mathfrak m_R$. Finally $vu=fq$: both are ring maps $R\to B$ restricting to $fq|_{\Lambda_A}$ on $\Lambda_A$ (as $v u(\lambda)=v_0\pi\varphi(\lambda)=v_0\varphi(\lambda)$), both send $X_i$ to $fq(X_i)=v_0\varphi(X_i)$ (as $\pi(\varphi(X_i)+Y_i)=\varphi(X_i)$), and both are continuous from the $(X)$-adic to the $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology ($u$ by the lemma and $v(\mathfrak m_S^N)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B^N$; $fq((X)^N)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B^N$ as $fq$ is local). $B$ is $\mathfrak m_B$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], so the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] ($T=B$, $I=\mathfrak m_B$) gives $vu=fq$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NN, proof, last paragraph ('Finally, we replace $\varphi$ by the map $\varphi'$ ...')

proof.text: (The parameters.) Write $a_i=\varphi(X_i)$, so $u(X_i)=a_i+Y_i$ and $a_i\in\mathfrak m_{S_0}$ (step 2), i.e. $a_i\in(Z_1,\ldots,Z_e)S$ resp. $(p,Z_1,\ldots,Z_e)S$ by step 1. Consider the elements $u(t_1),\ldots,u(t_d),Z_1,\ldots,Z_e$ of $S$: in the field case they are $a_1+Y_1,\ldots,a_n+Y_n,Z_1,\ldots,Z_e$; in the Cohen case $u(t_1)=u(p)=p$ (a unital ring map fixes $p$) and they are $p,a_1+Y_1,\ldots,a_n+Y_n,Z_1,\ldots,Z_e$. The ideal they generate contains the $Z_j$ (and $p$), hence every $a_i$, hence every $Y_i=(a_i+Y_i)-a_i$; so it is $\mathfrak m_S$ (step 3). Their number is $n+e$ resp. $n+1+e$, which is $\dim S$ (step 3). By [def-weil-regular-scheme] a set of $\dim S$ generators of $\mathfrak m_S$ is a regular system of parameters, so $u(t_1),\ldots,u(t_d)$ extend (by $Z_1,\ldots,Z_e$) to a regular system of parameters of $S$, with $t_1=p$ in residue characteristic $p$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NN, proof, last sentence ('it is clear that a regular system of parameters of $R$ maps to part of a regular sequence in $S'$'), and statement (4); $t_1=p$: proof of Proposition Tag 07NQ

proof.text: (Flatness and the closed fibre.) By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] applied to $S$ and the regular system of step 4 listed as $u(t_1),\ldots,u(t_d),Z_1,\ldots,Z_e$, this list is a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] and $S/(u(t_1),\ldots,u(t_d))$ is a regular local ring of dimension $\dim S-d$ (case $c=d$). Hence the initial segment $u(t_1),\ldots,u(t_d)$ is a regular sequence: its nonzerodivisor conditions are among those of the whole list, and $S/(u(t_1),\ldots,u(t_d))\ne0$ since it is local. Now $u:R\to S$ is a local map of Noetherian local rings (step 3), $R$ is regular of dimension $d$ with $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ generating $\mathfrak m_R$ (step 1), so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular] proves $u$ flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Since $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ generate $\mathfrak m_R$, $\mathfrak m_RS=(u(t_1),\ldots,u(t_d))S$, so $S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is regular local. This also covers $d=0$.

lead_note: 2026-10-10 L: refines lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-map-regular-presentation (07NN, split): that node gives R, S regular complete with the parameters; this one adds that R, S are power-series rings over fields or Cohen rings with t_1 = p. split_report.summary: Proof in 5 steps following Stacks 07NN (read with 07NL, 07NJ, 032A, 00R4, 00NU and the proof of 07NQ for t_1=p). The lead note asked to cite lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-map-regular-presentation for R, S; its statement does not say that R and S are power-series rings over fields or Cohen rings (that is only in its proof), and a regular complete local ring need not be such a power-series ring (ramified case: p in m^2), so its statement cannot give this node and is not cited (C3: no use of a proof). Instead the construction is done from statements: Cohen presentations of A and B (lem-weil-pbc-cohen-power-series-presentation, which gives t_1=p), the formal-smoothness lift, S = Lambda_B[[Y,Z]] with u(X_i)=phi(X_i)+Y_i, and flatness/fibre from the parameter nodes. Step 4 replaces the regular-presentation node's substitution automorphism by the direct observation that u(t), Z generate m_S and are dim S in number. No new nodes. No slopmaster2 Lean (grep by id, 07NN, Cohen, power series).

reviewed: 2026-10-10 L: 5 steps rebuilding 07NN from the Cohen presentation node (the regular-presentation node states only regularity, not the power-series form: the worker was right not to cite it), the lift by formal smoothness, S = Lambda_B[[Y, Z]] with vu = fq by the universal property, the parameters, flatness and the regular fibre; 0 new nodes. 07NN is stated three times (flat, regular, power-series form), the stronger implying the weaker: a later merge.

lean.statement: theorem exists_complete_local_map_cohen_presentation {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A] [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) B] (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f] : ∃ (ΛA ΛB : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing ΛA) (_ : CommRing ΛB) (n m : ℕ), let R := MvPowerSeries (Fin n) ΛA let S := MvPowerSeries (Fin m) ΛB ∃ (_ : IsRegularLocalRing R) (_ : IsRegularLocalRing S), IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R ∧ IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S) S ∧ (CharZero (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) → IsField ΛA ∧ IsField ΛB) ∧ (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → CharP (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) p → IsCohenRing p ΛA ∧ IsCohenRing p ΛB) ∧ ∃ (q : R →+* A) (v : S →+* B) (u : R →+* S), Function.Surjective q ∧ IsLocalHom q ∧ Function.Surjective v ∧ IsLocalHom v ∧ IsLocalHom u ∧ v.comp u = f.comp q ∧ u.Flat ∧ IsRegularLocalRing (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map u) ∧ ∃ (t : List R) (z : List S), IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters t ∧ IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters (t.map u ++ z) ∧ (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → CharP (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) p → t.head? = some (p : R))
